name: Energy performance contract: shared savings
summary: The ESCO finances and delivers the project and is repaid with an agreed share of the energy savings over a fixed period. The ESCO carries financing and performance risk.
how_it_makes_money: Pre-agreed percentage of verified savings for a fixed number of years; a larger share goes to the ESCO because of the up-front investment.

hardware: Efficiency measures installed by the ESCO
regulation: Accounting treatment of the contract (on or off balance sheet)
financing: ESCO funds the project from its own funds or loans and carries credit risk

stakeholder_value.customer: No up-front investment; pays out of savings
stakeholder_value.provider: Share of savings over the term
stakeholder_value.other: Lenders to the ESCO bear credit risk

what_must_be_true: Savings can be measured credibly and customers do not contest them
Savings are large enough to repay the ESCO's investment within the term
Customer accepts a larger savings share going to the provider

risks_failure_causes.text: Owners have an incentive to challenge measured savings to reduce payments
ESCO-financed projects are more expensive and less capital efficient for the provider
More complex contracts than guaranteed savings; accounting treatment issues

cases.note: Shared savings is used in over 75 percent of contracts according to the IEA.
Guaranteed savings is more common in Europe than shared savings. A 2013 US state document notes that shared savings is rarely favored by owners.

sources.title: Hawaii State Energy Office: Pros and cons of guaranteed vs shared energy savings (2013)
